source_title: Ofcom Adults Media Use and Attitudes 2026
unit_or_scope: UK adult internet and social-media users
direct_observation: Social-media use remained widespread but active posting sharing or commenting fell from 61 percent in 2024 to 49 percent; qualitative users described selective posting ephemeral content app deletion and leaving phones behind
missing_stage: wellbeing safety relationship voice and unequal withdrawal capacity
next_test: follow cohort across posting reduction control use exposure and later outcome

direct_observation: Adults spent about 4.5 hours online daily and online benefits remained majority-supported but declined; children used platforms for connection and wellbeing while reporting doomscrolling concerns
missing_stage: durable wellbeing exposure reduction and social participation
next_test: compare active passive private and harmful encounters over time

unit_or_scope: more than 3650 UK adults in experiment
direct_observation: Granular content-control choices led more than seven in ten participants to use controls to reduce sensitive-content exposure; wording alone had no impact
missing_stage: live-platform persistence exposure reduction subgroup effect and later trust
next_test: match experimental control uptake to live exposure and repeat use

unit_or_scope: UK adolescents and adults in mock platform experiment
direct_observation: Safe-by-design defaults received strong support and high retention while adult acceptance varied with default configuration
missing_stage: real-world persistence false reassurance participation and subgroup effect
next_test: observe live default retention and social opportunity cost

source_title: Pew teens social media and mental health 2025
direct_observation: 44 percent reported cutting back on social-media use and an identical share reported cutting back on smartphone use
missing_stage: cause duration substitution social cost and later wellbeing or school/relationship outcome
next_test: repeat panel with measured use and non-use reasons

direct_observation: Reported use remained broad across YouTube Facebook Instagram TikTok WhatsApp Reddit and X
missing_stage: active versus passive/private use benefit harm and dependence
next_test: disaggregate use mode and platform dependence by subgroup
